newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares fall in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares fall in quiet trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell for a fifth consecutive day on Tuesday, dragged down by losses in industrial stocks in the quietest trade for a month.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped to 151.56 points in business worth just 373,000 dinars ($527,000).

It was the lowest trading volume since sanction-hit Iraq announced last month it had reached agreement with the United Nations to resume limited oil exports, raising business hopes in neighbouring Jordan.
National Industries, one of the firms expected to benefit from the U.N. oil-for-food deal, fell back 0.04 dinars to 0.73 in the heaviest business of the day, worth a total 59,000 dinars.
Jordan Cement Factory JOCM.A and Jordan Electric Power fell back 0.02 dinars and 0.01 dinars in moderate trade.
"It's still quiet and it should stay that way," said Samir Jaradat of Jordan Investment Finance Bank.
Insurance company Al-Nisr al-Arabi bucked the trend to rise five percent to 5.34 dinars on expectations that the one million dinar capitalised firm could issue a 20 percent cash dividend.
Falling shares outnumbered gainers on Tuesday by 28 to nine, with shares in six other firms trading but closing unchanged.
